title: Summary Statistics for Two Categorical Variables
rights: Original teacher-authored public-safe practice; no secure assessments.

items.prompt: What is the joint relative frequency of App and Tea?
items.hint: Identify the correct group first; then determine the numerator and denominator.
items.solution: The intersection count is 2 and the grand total is 24: 2/24.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

items.prompt: What is the marginal relative frequency of Tea?
items.hint: Identify the correct group first; then determine the numerator and denominator.
items.solution: The Tea column margin is 10 out of the grand total 24.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

items.prompt: What fraction of App orders were Tea?
items.hint: Identify the correct group first; then determine the numerator and denominator.
items.solution: The App row total is 8, and two of these orders were Tea: 2/8.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

items.prompt: What percentage of Tea orders came through App?
items.hint: Identify the correct group first; then determine the numerator and denominator.
items.solution: The Tea column total is 10, with 2 App entries: 2/10=20%.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

items.prompt: Which Tea percentages should be compared by channel?
items.hint: Identify the correct group first; then determine the numerator and denominator.
items.solution: Within each channel Tea shares are 2/8=25% and 8/16=50%.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

items.prompt: What statement is supported by these observations?
items.hint: Identify the correct group first; then determine the numerator and denominator.
items.solution: Conditional drink proportions differ by channel, an association within these 24 records; causation and population generalization are not justified.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

options.label: A
options.text: Drink type and ordering channel are associated in this table, without proven causation.

options.label: B
options.text: Using App causes customers to buy Coffee.

options.label: C
options.text: No association exists because Coffee counts are equal.

options.label: D
options.text: All cafés have the same drink mix.

items.prompt: Four Coffee orders came through each channel. What is the valid within-channel comparison?
items.hint: Identify the correct group first; then determine the numerator and denominator.
items.solution: For App the denominator is 8 and for Counter 16, so 4/8=50% versus 4/16=25%.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

items.prompt: Among Coffee orders, what fraction came through Counter?
items.hint: Identify the correct group first; then determine the numerator and denominator.
items.solution: The reference group contains 8 Coffee orders; 4 are Counter, giving 4/8.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026
